(but rather an interjection) please; as you wish; (or as if voc.) sir! lord! my lady ! sirs ! [ BHS bhadrakalpa], an excellent, auspicious, aeon; D II 2, 21 (imasmiṃ yeva kho ~e); It-a I 29, 26 (imasmiṃ ~e amhākaṃ bhagavato kāle); Ap-a 542, 7 (ayaṃ kappo Kakusandho Koṇāgamano Kassapo Gotamo Metteyyo ti pañcabuddhapaṭimaṇḍitattā ~o nāma jāto); Bv-a 191, 25 (yasmiṃ kappe pañca buddhā uppajjanti so ~o); Cp-a 1, 14 (imasmiṃ ~asmiṃ); — °- kumbha , m. [bhadda + kumbha 2 ], an auspicious jar; Abh 359 (~o puṇṇakumbho); — °- dāru , m. , the tree deodar; SAF: Cedrus deodara (Roxb.) D.Don; Abh 568 (devadāru ~u); — °- pada , n. , — ifc see uttara- ( sv uttara 1 ), pubba- ( sv pubba 2 ); — °- pīṭha , n. [bhadda + pīṭha 2 ], a woven, wicker seat; Abh 311 (kocchaṃ tu ~e); Vin II 149, 30 (~aṃ uppannaṃ hoti; Sp 1216, 25 : ~an ti sabbavettamayaṃ pīṭhaṃ vuccati); Ja III 410, 18 (devī … kañcanabhaddapīṭhaṃ attharitvā); IV 281, 8 (mahāsattaṃ … ~e nisīdāpetvā); Vv-a 8, 29 (~an ti ettha vettalatādīhi upavītaṃ āsanaṃ); 30, 6 (tadā mama santike vijjamānaṃ ~aṃ, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee bhaddaṃ pīṭhaṃ); — °- pīṭhaka , n. , id.; Sp 45, 1 (ekacce ~esu … nisīdiṃsu); — °- mukha , ( and more often ) bhadramukha, mf ( n ). [ S. bhadramukha], ‘whose face confers prosperity’; usually voc.: good sir; good people; M I 282, 15 (ehi tvaṃ bhadramukha saṅghāṭiko hohi); II 53, 27 (haratha bhante haratha bhadramukhā ti); S I 74, 21 (bhadramukho dāni atthakaraṇena paññāyissatī ti; Spk I 139, 22 : sundaramukho); Ja II 261, 14 (kiṃ bhadramukhā jānittha pañhan ti, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se ~ā); III 38, 26´ (ehi bhadramukha uddesaṃ gaṇha aṭṭhakathaṃ suṇa); V 171, 15´ (~assa Saṅkhapālanāgassa idaṃ sampattijātaṃ, Ce, Se so; Be, Ee bhadra-); Vism 92, 21 (atha naṃ thero pucchi kiṃ ~a diṭṭhā te upāsikā ti, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee bhadra-); — °- mutta , °-muttaka, m.n. [ cf S. lex. bhadramusta, bhadramustaka], nut grass; SAF: Cyperus rotundus L.; Abh 599 (gundā ca ~aṃ); Vin IV 35, 2 (mūlabījaṃ nāma haliddi … usīraṃ °-muttakaṃ); Ja VI 537, 21* (unnakā ~ā ca, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se °-muṭṭhā); Vin-vn 1327 (~aṃ); — °- latā , f. [ cf S. lex. bhadralatā], a kind of creeper, perhaps Hiptage benghalensis (l.) Kurz; Sv 868, 36 (badālatā ti ekā madhurarasā ~ā); — °- sāla , m. , a kind of (sal) tree; Vin I 352, 27 (~-mūle) = S III 95, 17 = Ud 41, 19 (Ud-a 250, 7 : ~o ti pana tatth’ eko manāpo bhaddako sālarukkho, Be, Se so; Ce laddhako sālarukkho; Ee laṭṭhako sālarukkho); Ja IV 156, 4´ (~-rukkhena); — abhadda , mfn. , not good; bringing misfortune; Paṭis-a 443, 14 (āyatiṃ ~-tāya ahitaṃ).

(~ena ca sīlena bhaddikāya ca diṭṭhiyā); Pv 1:3 (kammaṃ katvāna ~aṃ); Th 391 (so virūhati saddhamme khette bījaṃ va ~aṃ); Ja I 115, 29 (mayhaṃ sakalalokassāpi tav’ eva pabbajjā bhaddikā); 269, 31* (na cāyaṃ bhaddikā surā); III 182, 20 (~ena nakkhattena maṅgalakiriyaṃ katvā); IV 451, 4* (vipāko hoti bhadrako); Nidd I 365, 18 (sundaraṃ ~aṃ kalyāṇaṃ); Ap 34, 13 (tamh’ eva ~e kappe; Ap-a 267, 19 : pañcabuddhapaṭimaṇḍitattā ~e nāma kappe); Cp 2:5:3 (ṭhānaṃ addasa ~aṃ); Mil 375, 20 (bījaṃ … ~e khette vuttaṃ); Vism 312, 2 (supinaṃ passanto pi ~am eva supinaṃ passati); Mp I 169, 25 (amma ~e kāle āgatā si); Dhp-a I 214, 4 (~o vata no uttaribhaṅgo uppanno); III 446, 5 (~ena divasena); Ud-a 290, 12 (bhaddikā eva Suppabuddhassa gati na pāpikā ti, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee ~ā); Pj II 576, 12 (~o no rājā laddho bhaddikā rājaparisā ti); — 2. ( n. ) a good thing, good; good fortune; Ja III 252, 10 (sace … etth’ eva … imaṃ divasaṃ vaseyyaṃ bhadrakaṃ vata assā ti); Sv 866, 29 (~aṃ vat’ assa sace āloko pātubhaveyyā ti); Ps IV 6, 2 (~aṃ te bhadde kataṃ); Mp I 269, 20 (ahaṃ imaṃ mantaṃ uggaṇhitvā sakalajambudīpe jeṭṭhako bhavissāmi evaṃ sante tumhākaṃ pi ~aṃ bhavissatī ti, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee bhaddaṃ); Dhp-a II 246, 16 (~aṃ esa vadati); — bhadrakā in Ee at Ja V 254, 29* (bahū pi bhadrakā ete) is perhaps wr; Be, Ce, Se bahūni samaṇabhadrāni; — bhaddakassa in Ee at Dhp-a III 151, 4 is wr; Be bhatakassa; Ce, Se bhaṭakassa; — ifc see upari-; — abhaddaka , mfn. and n. , 1. ( mfn. ) not good; unpleasant; Ja V 480, 21´ (jīvitaṃ hi tassa āyatiṃ ~-ttā dujjīvitaṃ nāma, Se so; Ce anāyatibhaddakattā va; Ee anāyatabhadrakattā; Be different ); Ap 101, 13 (vācaṃ bhāsiṃ ~aṃ); Pv-a 114, 12 (pāpako ti ~o); Th-a II 186, 21 (~-taraṃ akalyāṇataraṃ); — 2. ( n. ) wrong-doing; mischief; Ud-a 426, 31 (pāpakaṃ ~aṃ … pajahati); Pv-a 116, 19 (pāpena ~ena aniṭṭhena bādhati); — atibhaddaka , atibhadraka, mfn. , very good; very auspicious; Mil 234, 28 (atibhadrakaṃ veyyākaraṇaṃ); Ps II 78, 31 (~o ayaṃ dhammapariyāyo); — subhaddaka , subhadraka, mfn. , very good; very fine; M III 268, 16 (~ā vat’ ime Sunāparantakā manussā yaṃ me na-y-ime pāṇinā pahāraṃ dentī ti) = S IV 61, 15 quoted Pj I 149, 11 ( Be, Se so; Ce, Ee subhadrakā); Ja III 82, 24* (catuppado ~o c’ eva supesalo ca); Ap 339, 12 (~o tvaṃ manuja); 547, 24 (jiṇṇena dhammo ’yaṃ caritabbo ~o).

pn:
Bhadrāvudha. One of the sixteen disciples of Bāvarī, who, at his request, visited Gotama Buddha (Snp.vs.1008). He questioned the Buddha as to how a man could get over attachment and cross the flood. By grasping after nothing in the world, answered the Buddha, for Māra follows the man who clings to things.

This question and answer are contained in the Bhadrāvudhamāṇavapuccha (Snp.vs.1101-4), which is explained in the Cūḷa Niddesa (CNid.36f).

At the end of the discourse, Bhadrāvudha and his pupils became Arahants and joined the Saṅgha. Snp-a.ii.599.
